- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Looking at the configuration changes within the two-hour window before the first rejection (09:33:54–11:33:54 UTC), only one change stands out as directly relevant to the garnet-split component's failure mode:

**CHG-45710** (2026-02-18 10:33 UTC, team-Marten): `set split.max_pages_per_job: 1000 -> 40`

This change drastically lowered the maximum pages per job the splitter would accept (from 1000 down to 40). Looking at the journal, the "received" events show many incoming documents with page counts well above 40 (e.g., 20-30 pages is common, but some docs were being split into pieces exceeding 40 pages cumulatively, or likely the split logic uses this limit to determine if a document can be chunked). The rejection reason "document cannot be split" starting ~57 minutes after this change (10:33 → first retries at 11:27, first hard rejection at 11:33:54) is consistent with jobs queued before the change working through older oversized documents until the retry-exhaustion logic kicked in, producing cascading `retry` then `job-rejected` events.

All other components' changes in that window (tundra-scan's log_level change at 09:12, moss-notify's retry_backoff_ms change at 11:11) are either log-verbosity tweaks (no functional impact) or unrelated to the split-rejection pattern. The moss-notify change is also too late (11:11) relative to when retries began appearing (11:27) — though close in time, it doesn't explain the "document cannot be split" reason, which is specific to garnet-split's own capacity setting.

{"faulty_change": "CHG-45710"}

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

instruction_parts.content:
Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

instruction_parts.content:
Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Your tools give read-only access to the service's job-event journals, its configuration change history, queue statistics and the operations playbook. Use them to establish the facts.

Copy values verbatim from the tool output (no rounding or reformatting), and put no labels, notes or other text inside a value.

</task>

{"id": "t2.answer", "role": "assistant", "body": "Looking at the configuration changes within the two-hour window before the first rejection (09:33:54–11:33:54 UTC), only one change stands out as directly relevant to the garnet-split component's failure mode:

**CHG-45710** (2026-02-18 10:33 UTC, team-Marten): `set split.max_pages_per_job: 1000 -> 40`

This change drastically lowered the maximum pages per job the splitter would accept (from 1000 down to 40). Looking at the journal, the "received" events show many incoming documents with page counts well above 40 (e.g., 20-30 pages is common, but some docs were being split into pieces exceeding 40 pages cumulatively, or likely the split logic uses this limit to determine if a document can be chunked). The rejection reason "document cannot be split" starting ~57 minutes after this change (10:33 → first retries at 11:27, first hard rejection at 11:33:54) is consistent with jobs queued before the change working through older oversized documents until the retry-exhaustion logic kicked in, producing cascading `retry` then `job-rejected` events.

All other components' changes in that window (tundra-scan's log_level change at 09:12, moss-notify's retry_backoff_ms change at 11:11) are either log-verbosity tweaks (no functional impact) or unrelated to the split-rejection pattern. The moss-notify change is also too late (11:11) relative to when retries began appearing (11:27) — though close in time, it doesn't explain the "document cannot be split" reason, which is specific to garnet-split's own capacity setting.

```json
{"faulty_change": "CHG-45710"}
```", "protected": true}

instruction_parts.content:
Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

instruction_parts.content:
Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

instruction_parts.content:
Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.

instruction_parts.content:
Each request contains three sections:
- <task>: the fixed task. It is never edited and always present.
- <runtime_status>: limits and budget occupancy computed by the runtime.
- <working_context>: your transcript so far, one JSON object per line with id, role, body.
  This is the only memory you have between steps (apart from files you write).

You may call several tools in one step; they all run.
"edit_context" applies a list of operations to your working context, in order:
{"op": "delete", "ids": ["..."]}, {"op": "replace", "id": "...", "body": "..."} and
{"op": "add_note", "id": "...", "body": "..."}. A short result comes back as an observation entry.

CONTEXT EDITING (you control your working context):
- The entries in <working_context> are your working context. Whatever it contains after your
  step becomes <working_context> in the next request.
  ids: unique, 1-64 chars of [A-Za-z0-9_.:~-]; roles: assistant, observation, note, summary, receipt.
  Limits: 200 entries, 24000 chars per body.
- With the operations you may delete entries, rewrite or shorten bodies, and add notes.
- Entries marked protected (earlier requests and your earlier answers) can't be edited or deleted; tidy everything else as needed.
- Ordering rule: the context you see at the start of a step holds the context up to the previous
  step. After your step, the runtime validates the edit, then appends this step's action and
  observation (and a short receipt if you edited). Edits therefore cannot remove the current
  step's output; you can remove it in a later step.
- Invalid edits (unknown ids, duplicate ids, other roles, too large) are rejected and the previous
  context is kept. The task and these instructions are outside the context.
- Editing is optional. When <runtime_status> reports pressure, manage the context before it runs
  out. Keep exact values, file:line references and open questions you still need.
